Respo Prayer: Writ Petition is filed under Article 226 of the Constitutio India to issue a Writ in the nature of Declaration, declaring the Notification No.2/MRB/2021 dated 13.10.2021 insofar as Clause 6B, N prescribing the candidate should have studied Tamil as one of the s Hsc read with Corrigendum adding Sslc and Proceedings of the 2nd Respondent dated 13.03.2023 bearing No.02/MRB/2021 insofar as including the name of the Petitioner in the list of ineligible cand post of Food Safety Officers illegal and contrary to Section 21 of Nadu Government servants (Conditions of Service) Act, 2016 and consequently direct the Respondents to include the name of the Peti the provisional selection list for the post of Food Safety Officer appropriate place based on the marks secured by her in the Written on that basis consider her and appoint her in the post of Food Safe For Petitioner : Mr. Balan Haridas For Respondents : Mr.P. texts.facts: It is the case of the writ petitioner that she has secured second highest marks (82 marks) in the State. However, her name has not been found in the provisional list mainly on the ground that she has not studied Tamil Language in HSC.
texts.arguments: It is the contention of the Writ Petitioner that https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis W.P.No.9725 of 2023 and W.M.P.No.9804 of 2023 since her parents are working in Andaman she studied in Kendrya Vidyalaya, therefore, she could not study in Tamil. 3. It is the contention of the learned Counsel that in view of the Section 21 of the Tamil Nadu Government Servants (Conditions of Service) Act, 2016, the very notification can not be sustained in the eye of law. 4. It is not in dispute that the Petitioner has secured 82 marks and she has got degree in Food Processing Engineering and she is a post graduate. Her qualification is also found to be equivalent and recognised and notified by the Central Government as per the Notification. The only thing is put against the writ petitioner in the notification is that she should have studied Tamil language in HSC as Tamil is one of the subject in HSC in the State Board. 5. It is relevant to note that Section 21 of the Tamil Nadu Government Servants (Conditions of Service) Act, 2016, which is as follows: https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis W.P.No.9725 of 2023 and W.M.P.No.9804 of 2023 21.(1) No person shall be eligible for appointment to any service by direct recruitment unless he has an adequate knowledge of the official language of the State, namely, Tamil: Provided that a person, being otherwise qualified for appointment to the post to which recruitment is to be made, may apply for recruitment to the post, despite the fact that, at the time of such application, he does not possess an adequate knowledge of Tamil. Explanation. For the purpose of this section, a person shall be deemed to have an adequate knowledge of Tamil, if (i) in the case of a post for which the educational qualification prescribed is the minimum general educational qualification and above, he has passed the S.S.L.C. Examination or its equivalent examination with Tamil as one of the languages; or Studied the High School Course in Tamil medium and passed the S.S.L.C. Examination or its equivalent examination in Tamil medium; or passed the Second Class Language Test in Tamil conducted by the Commission; https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis W.P.No.9725 of 2023 and W.M.P.No.9804 of 2023 (ii) in the case of a post for which the educational qualification prescribed is VIII Standard and above, but below S.S.L.C., he has studied in Tamil medium in those standards or passed the S. Shiva Shankari vs Government Of Tamil Nadu on 25 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/96456770/ 3 Language Test in Tamil referred to in sub-section (1) of section 22; and (iii) in the case of a post for which the educational qualification prescribed is below VIII Standard, he has studied in Tamil medium in those standards or passed the oral test in Tamil referred to in sub-section (2) of section (2) Every such candidate as is referred to in the proviso to sub-section (1) shall, if selected and appointed on or after the 9th February 1996, pass the Second Class Language Test in Tamil conducted by the Commission, or pass the language Test in Tamil referred to in sub-section (1) of section 22 conducted by the appointing authority or pass the oral test referred to in sub-section (2) of section 22 conducted by the appointing authority, as the case may be, within a period of two years from the date of his appointment. If he fails to pass the said Language Test within the said period of two years, he shall be discharged from https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis W.P.No.9725 of 2023 and W.M.P.No.9804 of 2023 service. (3) The syllabus for the Second Class Language Test in Tamil referred to in this section shall be as specified in Schedule-IV 6. 7. As per Sub-Clause 2 of the Section 21 of the above Act makes it clear that even after appointment a person can pass test in Tamil within a period of two years from the date of his/her appointment.
